data.title: Bristol, Tempus AI partnering with Pathos AI to advance neurological treatments
data.description:
• Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY) will collaborate with Pathos AI to utilize the latter's agentic AI platform, Foundry, to build a specialized, curated dataset and agentic AI capabilities for Alzheimer’s disease and other neurological ailments.
  • Also, Bristol is the lead in the AI firm's Series E financing.
  • Though the three-year deal, "BMS aims to generate deeper insights into disease progression, identify patients most likely to benefit from potential therapies and design more precise clinical trials," per a news release.
  • Tempus AI (TEM) inked a separate deal with Pathos AI to apply the former's expertise in oncology "to create a comprehensive, de-identified, longitudinal dataset from hundreds of thousands of patients with neurological conditions, designed to track outcomes over time and accelerate biological insight." 
  • Terms call for Pathos to license the data from Tempus in a five-year, $55M agreement.

data.title: Comfort Systems USA drops 9% after earnings, CFO retirement
data.description:
Shares of Comfort Systems USA (FIX), a mechanical and electrical contracting services company, retreated just over 9% on Friday after the company posted third-quarter results. The company beat consensus estimates yet still failed to reassure investors about whether current valuations leave room for further gains.

FIX closed at $1,160.86, a decline of $118.51, as volume reached approximately 1.37 million shares, roughly 3.6 times the one-month average. This added to a recent retreat, including a nearly 9% drop on Thursday.

data.title: Corcept Therapeutics plunges 20% on Genmab cancer data
data.description:
Shares of Corcept Therapeutics (CORT), a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on cortisol modulation, sank 20% on Friday. The stock dropped $21.64 to end at $85.86 with volume of roughly 2.86 million shares, a relative volume of 3.78 times the one-month average.

The slide came after Genmab reported that a phase 3 trial of its antibody-drug conjugate, rinatabart sesutecan (Rina-S), met its primary goal for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. CORT, which markets Lifyorli (relacorilant) for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, dropped on the news.

data.title: IC Group restructures leadership, targets $900K in annual savings
data.description:
• IC Group (ICGH:CA) announced a leadership restructuring on Friday, with COO Marc Caron departing and other non-officer positions eliminated, effective immediately.
  • The company expects a Q4 FY2026 restructuring charge of approximately $1M, mainly for severance and employee transition costs.
  • The changes are expected to generate annual savings of approximately $900K.
  • CEO Duncan McCready said the changes aim to simplify decision-making, improve accountability, and focus resources on key growth priorities.
  • The restructuring charge is expected to be paid over the next 14 months.

data.title: Gentherm surges 9%, bouncing back after recent slide
Defensive-led market breadth is a warning sign, not a win - Carson
data.description:
Carson Group is warning investors that the long-awaited expansion in market breadth may have arrived with a painful catch—it's being driven by defensive sectors while AI stocks are in freefall.

On Thursday, 324 of 500 S&P 500 (SPY) (VOO) companies increased, with the median stock climbing 1.09%, Carson noted in a blog post published Friday. Yet the S&P 500 itself fell 1.36%, technology (XLK) plunged 3.3%, and the Goldman Sachs Broad AI Index dropped 6.01%. Nine of 11 sectors beat the index, with defensive plays—staples (XLP), utilities (XLU), and health care (XLV)—leading the way.

The shift has been dramatic. On June 22, AI stocks (AIQ) (AIEQ) were outperforming non-AI stocks by 49 percentage points year-to-date. That lead has collapsed to just 4.8 points.

Through Thursday, non-AI stocks have outperformed AI by over 28 percentage points in the second half of 2026.

The concentration problem is acute. Technology alone represents 38% of the S&P 500, and adding Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL), Meta (META), Amazon (AMZN), and Tesla (TSLA) pushes AI-linked exposure past 51%, Carson said. In the first half of 2026, when the S&P 500 returned 10.2%, the AI basket contributed 75% of that gain despite averaging only 37% of index weight.

That dynamic has reversed. In the second half, the AI basket—now 39% of the index—has subtracted 1.7 percentage points from S&P 500 returns, while non-AI stocks contributed 4.2 points.

Carson pointed out that that rotation marked the end of the late 1990s tech bubble and warned that if the current pattern persists, it could signal the end of both the AI wave and the broader bull market.

data.title: Gilead in $45M settlement with Texas over alleged Medicaid kickback scheme
data.description:
• Gilead Sciences (GILD) will pay Texas $45M to settle allegations that it provided illegal incentives to medical providers to prescribe their drugs over their rivals for Medicaid patients.
  • Attorney General Ken Paxton said that Gilead provided "free nurses" and reimbursement support services to healthcare workers.
  • Paxtion added that Gilead's conduct violated the Texas Health Care Program Fraud Prevention Act
